To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the δ 18 O record from the Bromide–Viola Spring Formations in southernmost Oklahoma is inconsistent with previous hypotheses that global cooling occurred in the uppermost Sandbain and lower Katian across Laurentia.

(1) the Sandbian–lowermost Katian conodont δ 18 O record from southern Oklahoma is inconsistent with a major cooling event at the Sandbian– Katian boundary; (2) a short-lived cooling interval is present within the lower part of the GICE that is consistent with a short-lived drawdown in atmospheric p CO 3 ; and (3) the upper GICE conodont apatites record a mean temperature of 22–24°C.
